selected_mechanism.name: NTIA BEAD Supplemental Deployment Policy Notice (savings 'true-up' redeployment)

news_trigger.what_happened: The Commerce Department announced it would "accept new proposals from states under the Broadband Equity, Access and Deployment program" targeting "newly identified unserved locations" that became eligible due to FCC map changes or program defaults. NTIA Administrator Roth "visited Alaska and attended a roundtable with broadband providers," and Sen. Dan Sullivan stated "the new round could make 'over 5,000' new locations eligible for broadband deployment funding in his state."

selected_mechanism.one_line_definition: A September 2026 NTIA policy notice lets state broadband offices redeploy unspent BEAD 'Benefit of the Bargain' savings to fund builds at locations missing or mis-mapped in the first round, on a re-bid-then-reapprove cycle the NTIA Administrator must approve before any funds can be drawn.

layers.name: FCC Broadband Serviceable Location Fabric / National Broadband Map (eligibility trigger)
layers.what_it_does: The FCC's biannual updates to the location fabric and coverage map are what create 'newly identified unserved locations' — the statutory definition of who becomes BEAD-eligible for the supplemental round.
layers.controlling_actor: The Commission (Federal Communications Commission), per its statutory duty to build the location fabric and identify unserved areas

primary_source.outlet: U.S. Code (Office of the Law Revision Counsel)

layers.name: NTIA BEAD approval & reallocation authority (Supplemental Deployment Policy Notice)
layers.what_it_does: NTIA issues the supplemental policy notice and approves or disapproves each state's supplemental final proposal, and holds statutory power to reallocate or deobligate unspent 'Benefit of the Bargain' savings before draw-down.
layers.controlling_actor: Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Communications and Information / NTIA Administrator (current incumbent Arielle Roth)

primary_source.outlet: U.S. Code (Office of the Law Revision Counsel)

layers.name: Subgrantee deployment in rural Alaska
layers.what_it_does: Awarded providers build the last/middle-mile fiber and wireless to unserved rural Alaska locations; their rural construction is explicitly conditioned on BEAD/IIJA subsidy availability.
layers.controlling_actor: GCI Holdings (subsidiary of GCI Liberty), described in filings as 'the leading integrated communication services provider' in Alaska and a BEAD subgrantee for rural builds

primary_source.outlet: SEC EDGAR (GCI Liberty, Inc. Form 10-K, FY2025, filed 2026-02-11)

selected_mechanism.chokepoint: Layer 2 — the Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Communications and Information (NTIA Administrator) unilaterally approves or disapproves Alaska's supplemental final proposal and can reallocate or deobligate the roughly $370M+ in Alaska's unspent BEAD savings under 47 U.S.C. 1702(c)(5)(C) and (g)(3). One statutory officer owns the approve/reject/reallocate binary; the FCC (map) and the state broadband office are upstream, but the money gate sits at this single desk — not a committee.
selected_mechanism.ak_consequence: Rural Alaska broadband/connectivity: whether ~5,000+ newly-mapped unserved Alaska locations and the ~$370M+ of Alaska's unspent BEAD savings get funded hinges on the NTIA Administrator's approval of Alaska's supplemental final proposal this fall (notice issued 2026-09-03), directly gating GCI Holdings' BEAD-dependent rural builds.
selected_mechanism.structural_read: This is a funding-deployment vehicle whose entire flow narrows to one statutory officer. The FCC decides who counts as 'unserved,' but the NTIA Administrator decides whether Alaska's leftover savings may chase those locations at all — an approve/reject/reallocate power that persists no matter who holds the office. AI nexus: last- and middle-mile connectivity to newly-unserved rural Alaska is the physical substrate for any AI workload outside the Railbelt — edge compute, satellite/remote-sensing pipelines, and telehealth or resource-monitoring inference all die at the point where fiber and fixed wireless stop. Redeploying $370M+ of savings to 5,000+ Bush locations is, structurally, a decision about where Alaska AI can be deployed at all; the mechanism produces a single-desk gate over rural Alaska's AI-connectivity backbone.
selected_mechanism.forward_implication: This week, a rural-connectivity or edge-compute allocator/operator should map exposure to GCI Holdings' BEAD-dependent rural Alaska builds and treat the NTIA Administrator's approval of Alaska's supplemental final proposal (submissions triggered by the 2026-09-03 notice, decision expected this fall) as the binary gating ~$370M of deployable capital — confirm which locations the state expects to put in the supplemental proposal before that submission window closes, rather than assuming first-round awards define the footprint.

_validation_note: Overlap resolved: the vehicles and regulatory framings of the NTIA BEAD supplemental notice were treated as one mechanism; the most asymmetric chokepoint is the NTIA Administrator's unilateral approve/reject/reallocate authority (not the Alaska Broadband Office's upstream selection), so leverage — not novelty — decided the framing. Category set to VEHICLES because the mechanism is a federal grant-deployment vehicle and the coverage note (regulatory saturated 3/6, vehicles absent 6 issues) tips a label choice that does not affect accuracy (the chokepoint is identical under either label). ACCESS LIMITATION, disclosed for the Editor's note: the actual NTIA Supplemental Deployment Policy Notice PDF could not be fetched (persistent HTTP 503 across every ntia.gov and broadbandusa.ntia.gov path — both scouts and the validator failed), and fcc.gov, broadbandmap.fcc.gov, and commerce.alaska.gov all returned 403. Rather than cite unfetched pages, each surviving layer was re-anchored to a fetched primary: 47 U.S.C. 642 (FCC mapping duty), 47 U.S.C. 1702 (NTIA Administrator's statutory approve/reallocate authority = chokepoint), and the GCI Liberty FY2025 10-K (provider layer, filed 2026-02-11; note GCI was divested from Liberty Broadband on 2025-07-14, so GCI Liberty — not Liberty Broadband — is the correct filer). The unverifiable Alaska Broadband Office director name (Thomas Lochner) was NOT shipped, and the ABO and NIST layers were dropped for lack of a fetchable primary source; dropping them does not break the FCC->NTIA->GCI chain or the chokepoint. The notice's issuance and terms are corroborated by two fetched, in-window news sources (Roll Call 2026-09-04; Telecompetitor 2026-09-03). Window NOT broadened; selection made at 14 days.
